title: Atomic field-path register — Game Representation Specification revision 4
version: 2, after the stage A review (fidelity and determinism; the review did not look at slice items)

rowKinds.COLLECTION: The existence and count of elements in a collection. Items on a COLLECTION row say that elements matching a selector exist (EXISTS), how many (COUNT/RANGE), or that none may (NOT_EXISTS).
rowKinds.FIELD: An atomic property of one element, or of the game for non-collection rows.
rowKinds.VIEW: Computed from other rows, never stored. Items may constrain a view (checked in Gate B forward); a view never needs support and supports no stored row. Every contract still declares it.

fillableIsExhaustive: A free choice (REALIZATION) is possible only on rows with a 'fillable' entry, and only as that entry says (proposal P-4, applied for this run). sourceKinds is descriptive and licenses nothing.

rows.lateralValues: closed list (draft, AM-17), each with its interval test against the element's position.across, on an envelope of width W with the midline at W/2. wide-left: touches the 0 touchline and does not contain the midline. wide-right: touches the W touchline and does not contain the midline. wide: either of those. central: contains the midline and touches neither touchline. full-width: touches both touchlines. An element matching none carries no lateral value. A lateral selector identifies an existing region; it never creates one (AM-13 preserved)

comparison.note: AM-16 as extended by Christian, 20 September: a contract may author a comparative claim between represented game properties. Requirement kind COMPARES.
comparison.form: { row, selector (the left element), operator, rightRow, rightSelector }, operator in { =, !=, <, <=, >, >= }
comparison.relation: NARROWS. Never written with EXCLUSION strictness: a comparative is a relationship, not a prohibition [C20]. It never entails a value and never entails existence
comparison.reachesLine: Reduce the comparison by the stated derivation rules; where it reduces to a bound on ONE property the game holds, it reaches that property's line. Otherwise the line of its left operand. Otherwise no line, and it is reported not evaluable in the forward list only. Two comparatives that reach one line and that no single value satisfies collide (derivation spec s4.4 and s6). Added after the rerun; unratified, and flagged to Christian because SD-22 may not cover it
comparison.boundary: Both operands must be properties the resolved game contains and can evaluate. Never an inferred player state or ecological outcome: not pressure, opportunity, affordance availability, difficulty or uncertainty
comparison.evaluability: A comparison is evaluable only when both operands resolve to a value the game holds, or to a value derived by a stated rule from rows the game holds. Otherwise it is reported not evaluable, never quietly true
comparison.effectiveValue: For value comparisons over regions: the effective value of a region is the primary event's base value (V2) as changed by the magnitude (V9) of each value modifier whose referents include that region. A region no modifier names takes the base value. This derivation is this specification's reading, flagged for Christian. OPEN: V9's own kind is not fixed - multiplier or increment - and the two give different bounds for the same claim (>1 vs >0). Flagged, not chosen
comparison.operandForm: OPEN, and it matters. AM-16's adopted form makes both operands a register row plus selector, but no row holds a region's value, so Christian's own first example value(A) > value(B) cannot be written in the adopted form without either a derived operand (effectiveValue) or a new row. The rerun's items used a derived operand. His ruling needed
comparison.notAnExclusion: A comparative claim is not translated into a mutual exclusion. 'Wide has greater task value than central' is a relationship; it is not 'central value is forbidden' [C20]

relativeTerms.note: Interval tests for relative positions (RC-21). The referent must be a game element; if it is players or play, the item is OUTSIDE_BOUNDARY.
relativeTerms.beyond X (for team T): the element's near edge is at or past X's far edge, in T's attacking direction
relativeTerms.own end (of team T): touches the end line T defends
relativeTerms.attacking end (of team T): touches the end line T attacks
relativeTerms.central: contains the axis midline across the width, and touches neither touchline
relativeTerms.lengthwise: the element's extent along the axis is at least its extent across it (AM-22; renamed from 'longitudinal' to avoid colliding with the lateral selector attribute)
